authority: Human Owner: visual 3 is our kappa channel, the gap
question: Can a Kappa support-distance channel abstain on constant-count motion, a behavior absent from classifier training, without rejecting more than 5% of known LIFE behavior rows?
dependency: CA-IDENT-05 discovered constant-count motion as a novel holdout class and registered the reverse-weighted Memory-dominant metric as the strongest control
holdout_transform: quarter-turn id mod 4 plus fixed shift [5,-4]
known_training_policy: Rows labelled constant-count motion are excluded from classifier and Kappa calibration; all other behavior classes are known.
metric: P_reverse from CA-IDENT-05: squared distance contribution 1/64 radial Fourier plus 63/64 Shadow Memory after per-view standardization and dimension normalization
classifier: deterministic 3-nearest-neighbour with lexicographic tie break on known training rows
kappa_definition: kappa(x) is the minimum registered P_reverse squared distance from x to any known training row
threshold_calibration: For every known training row, compute nearest P_reverse squared distance to a known row with a different seed id. Tau is the nearest-rank 99th percentile of these leave-one-seed-out distances.
decision: Return ABSTAIN_UNKNOWN when kappa(x) > tau; otherwise return the deterministic 3-nearest-neighbour known-class prediction.
coverage_gate: The untouched evaluation bank must contain at least 10 registered-unknown rows and at least 10 rows for every known training class.
primary_gate: With coverage passing, registered-unknown recall must be at least 0.50 and known-row specificity (one minus false-abstain rate) must be at least 0.95.
secondary_record: Record Fourier-versus-Memory classifier disagreement separately as a seam indicator; it is descriptive and not part of the primary gate.
interpretation: Kappa is an abstention and residual channel at the representation seam. It is not a forced class, new carrier, physical field or proof that the unknown has been identified.
